briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for September 6, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 The Threat of Extreme Weather and Compound Disasters Striking the Globe
sections.content: Recently, simultaneous extreme weather phenomena have intensified globally, with severe impacts emerging. Record-breaking heatwaves in Europe and torrential downpours, akin to 'water bombs,' in Asia are making extreme weather commonplace, acting as an economic trigger [7, 15]. Particularly, as floods and droughts worsen, countries like Kazakhstan are facing emergencies in water security, highlighting the urgent need for a global overhaul of water management systems [5, 17]. Such extreme weather disproportionately affects vulnerable populations, underscoring the necessity of 'climate welfare' [6], and warnings are also being issued that climate change and food scarcity could increase conflict risks [42]. Furthermore, with ocean temperatures rising to record levels due to climate change and El Niño phenomena [41, 43], experts suggest that the world may have less time than anticipated to respond to climate change [44].

sections.title: ⚠️ Changes and Challenges Across Domestic Ecosystems and Industries
sections.content: Domestically, direct impacts of climate change are also being observed across various sectors. Horticultural farms are facing difficulties due to climate change [4, 11], and significant changes are appearing in agricultural crops, such as an abundant harvest of Hallabong oranges on Ulleungdo, traditionally known as an island of wild vegetables [13]. Furthermore, climate change factors like rising temperatures are causing a nationwide widespread outbreak of pine wilt disease, necessitating urgent control measures [8, 14]. In the industrial sector, the expansion of AI data centers by the three major telecommunication companies is increasing the burden of carbon emission management [35], and climate change is presenting new challenges across our society, including increasing the risk of aviation disruptions and exposing reliability issues in nuclear power generation [38, 45, 46].

sections.title: 🌱 Expanding Domestic and International Efforts for Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Efforts for carbon neutrality and renewable energy transition to address the climate crisis are actively continuing both domestically and internationally. Various local governments, including Guri City [16, 18], Seodaemun-gu [21], and Gwacheon City [23], are actively pursuing region-led climate crisis responses and carbon-neutral transitions. Yesan County is playing a leading role, being the first in Chungnam to prepare a 'Greenhouse Gas Reduction Awareness Budget Statement' [26, 28]. In the industrial sector, SK E&C and Enlighten are collaborating on renewable energy projects such as solar power [29], and SK Chemicals is continuing active investments by expanding its solar power grid from factory rooftops to power plants [33]. Furthermore, Korea Southern Power Co. (KOSPO) plans to repatriate profits from overseas power generation projects for investment in renewable energy [31], and GS E&C is also pursuing new and renewable energy strategies [32], highlighting responsible climate actions by corporations.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Deepening Climate Policy Discussions and Exploring Future Response Strategies
sections.content: Policy and social discussions to overcome the climate crisis are also deepening. On the occasion of the 7th International Day of Clean Air for blue skies, the government and industry pledged to reduce air pollution and greenhouse gases, expressing their policy commitment [25]. A forum will be held in the National Assembly on the theme of 'Green Industry Development System under the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act and AI Climate Tech Talent Policy Challenges' [27], demonstrating the importance of climate technology advancement and human resource development. Furthermore, scientific recommendations, such as the necessity of 'strong methane reduction' to limit global warming to within 2 degrees Celsius [20], are being presented, leading to active exploration of ways to achieve specific reduction targets. Internationally, discussions on climate change legislation continue [37], but challenges in policy implementation also exist, as seen in cases like the invalidation of New York State's climate change superfund law [39]. These efforts will contribute to raising awareness of climate change and laying the policy foundation for a sustainable future.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing once again highlights the severity of the climate crisis and emphasizes the importance of diverse response efforts underway both domestically and internationally. It is crucial to remember that climate change is no longer a distant future problem, but a reality directly impacting our daily lives, industries, and ecosystems. This concludes today's climate briefing.
